answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, please do not double to 80 miles next week. Five weeks out from the race is the worst possible moment to jump from 40 to 80; the single biggest predictor of a bad marathon is a sudden spike in load in the final month. Your club mate built to 70 over months, not a week. We beat 3:45 by sharpening what you already have: one quality session, one long run, easy days actually easy. If you want more volume, we add 1 to 3 miles a week, not 40 in one jump. Trust the plan; the fitness is coming through clearly in the numbers.

new.analysis:
This was a model execution week. You followed every line of the plan, the marathon-pace block on Wednesday held 8:37/mi (right on 3:45 pace), and the 15-miler on Sunday was steady with only 5 bpm of drift. That is exactly what a planned step-down after the 20-miler should look like.

The one thing I am watching is heart rate on the long run. Average 146 with more than half the time in zone 3 says you were cruising at the top of easy; that is fine for 15 miles but will cost you late in an 18 or 20. On Sunday keep the first 12 miles under 150, then the pace block is allowed to lift it.

Where we go now: this is the last big push before we start to taper. Next Sunday is 18 miles with a chunk at marathon pace to rehearse race rhythm on tired legs. Expect one more 18 to 20 the week after, then volume starts coming down. Please do not add a second quality session or stack miles on the easy days to "catch up"; the risk-to-reward in the final month runs entirely one way.

Sleep at 7 hours, zero pain, two strength sessions, and feeling good into next week. Keep all of that steady and the race will take care of itself.
